Page 32 of the METI Interpretation PDF shows Article 17, paragraph 2, table 17-1. It gives three limits: 150/Ig as the base case; 300/Ig for more than 1 s up to 2 s; and 600/Ig for 1 s or less. Recalculation: 0.8 s is 1 s or less, so the limit is 600/Ig = 600/5 = 120 Ω. One third of that is 40 Ω, so choice (4) is confirmed.

Equivalent circuit: the 100 V source feeds Rb = 40 Ω in series with Rd in parallel with Rh = 6000 Ω. The current-division result Ih = 100Rd/[Rb(Rd+Rh)+RdRh] = 100Rd/(6040Rd+240000) is algebraically correct.
Setting Ih = 0.01 A gives 39.6Rd = 2400, so Rd ≈ 60.6 Ω. Checking Rd = 60 Ω gives 6000/602400 ≈ 9.96 mA, which confirms it.
Approximate method: the case voltage is 100Rd/(40+Rd) ≤ 6000 × 0.01 = 60 V, so Rd ≤ 60 Ω. This agrees with choice (5).

Body currents for each choice recalculated: Rd = 10 Ω gives 1000/300400 ≈ 3.33 mA. Rd = 15 Ω gives 1500/330600 ≈ 4.54 mA. Rd = 20 Ω gives 2000/360800 ≈ 5.54 mA. Rd = 30 Ω gives 3000/421200 ≈ 7.12 mA. All match the stated values.
